feature: Scope and SLA (Portal) — Feature #1661, Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/screens/Scope and SLA.dc.html. The real page in the rebuilt artifacts/portal (/scope-and-sla), wired to the two live customer-facing engine reads documented in Design/portal/design_handoff_full_site/docs/scope-and-sla-contract-pack.md (#2452): GET /api/portal/customer/sla-status and GET /api/portal/customer/scope-status. Page lives at artifacts/portal/src/pages/scope-and-sla.tsx; hooks/types at lib/scope-sla-api.ts / lib/scope-sla-types.ts. Registered in the sidebar as 'Scope and SLA', between Change Control and Risk Register.
notes: #2513 (runSlaEngineForTenant resolving customerId as a users.id instead of a tenant id, so sla-status always read empty) is CLOSED/complete as of this build — confirmed live in artifacts/api-server/src/lib/sla-engine.ts:279-286, which now applies customerId directly to the SLA tables exactly like the sibling runScopeCreepEngineForTenant. This manifest asserts the real post-fix response shape, not the pre-fix always-empty one.

The design's own .dc.html carries a dashed-amber caveat card citing #2513 as still-open ('Treat this card as unconfirmed until that fix lands'). That fix has already landed, so the wired page in this build DOES NOT carry that caveat forward — keeping it would show customers a stale warning about a bug that no longer exists. Everything else in the design (layout, both cards, the three-area breakdown, the ledger) is carried forward verbatim.
Both engines compute live on every call (contract pack §3) — there is no persisted 'last run' row for either route, so updatedAt is always 'now'.

Confirmed live against the local DB at build time: sla_timers and scope_creep_detections both have 0 rows for every tenant (`SELECT count(*) FROM sla_timers` / `scope_creep_detections`), so the entitled testbed tenant's real, honest response today is the on_track / zero-open-items state for both engines — the same shape §5/§6 of the contract pack describes as indistinguishable from a bug-masked one before the fix, and now genuinely just an empty state. This manifest's apiTests assert exactly that real, current shape rather than a scenario the local data can't produce.
ENV VARS required: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD — the same testbed Customer account other portal manifests (risk-register.json, change-control.json) already use.

textContains reads el.innerText / el.textContent, so every assertion below targets RENDERED text. Copy is final and reproduced verbatim from the component source (carried forward from the design's own strings), so these are reliable probes.

data-testid coverage: scope-and-sla-page, scope-and-sla-status, scope-and-sla-sla-card, scope-and-sla-scope-card — all real testids added on the built components as part of this manifest (none pre-existed).

apiTests.name: SETUP — log in as the testbed Customer account; extract the bearer.
A1 — sla-status responds 200 with the real, post-#2513-fix overall status (not a 400/500).
A2 — sla-status carries the real headline this build's page renders verbatim.
A3 — sla-status.updatedAt exists — both engines compute live on every call (contract pack §3), so this is always 'now', never a stored figure.
A4 — scope-status responds 200 with the real overall status.
A5 — scope-status carries the real headline this build's page renders verbatim.
A6 — scope-status.areas is always exactly 3 entries (contract pack §2) — the page never adds a fourth or hides an empty one.
A7 — extract the first area's label, which SS5 asserts against the page's real rendered text.
